Beyond Discrimination: A Matched-Control
Pathway Audit for Evaluating Pathway-Specific
Evidence in ECG Classifiers
Anonymous
Abstract—Background: ECG classifiers routinely achieve high
discrimination, yet may rely on clinically irrelevant signal regions.
Existing explanation methods rarely test whether disease-specific
regions dominate over matched anatomical controls, whether
pathway conclusions survive dataset shift, or whether results
are robust to the perturbation operator itself—sensitivity is not
specificity.
Methods: We propose a model-agnostic matched-control per￾turbation audit for evaluating pathway-specific evidence in ECG
classifiers—distinguishing disease-consistent signal use from cor￾related but non-specific features. The protocol compares targeted
perturbations against anatomically adjacent controls, adopts lin￾ear interpolation as a continuity-preserving perturbation to avoid
hard-boundary artifacts, and evaluates pathway specificity under
frozen-weight transfer to an independent cardiologist-validated
dataset. A preregistered operator-comparison battery character￾izes how operator choice affects conclusions. Per-model evidence￾classification rules—pathway-supported, evidence-limited, not
supported—standardize interpretation under operator depen￾dence and external transfer, assigning a tier to each (architecture,
disease) pair rather than aggregating across architectures. Five
diagnoses spanning timing, morphology, and rhythm pathways
serve as a case-study panel across four architectures and two
datasets.
Results: 1AVB is the anchor demonstration: although PR￾segment perturbation produces a large AUROC drop, matched
QRS controls reverse the interpretation, yielding negative
anatomical specificity under the primary linear-interpolation
operator (ResNet ASS= −0.332) and on the external dataset
(ASS= −0.278). This indicates that target-only perturbation can
produce false-positive pathway claims. A preregistered operator￾comparison battery shows that zero-masking creates boundary
artifacts that inflate control-region disruption; linear interpola￾tion is adopted as the primary operator. Under this protocol,
QRS-morphology pathways (CRBBB, CLBBB) reach Pathway￾supported on all three raw-signal architectures: internal positive

PTB-XL fold 10 under the same primary operator (CRBBB

CLBBB: 0.261/0.330/0.387). SBRAD reveals architecture het￾erogeneity: ResNet is Evidence-limited (rate pathway positive
internally and externally, ASS 0.092/0.111, but external CI

Conclusions: Standard discrimination metrics are insufficient
for evaluating whether a classifier uses disease-consistent signal
pathways under this audit. The matched-control audit protocol,
with explicit operator documentation and external transfer, can
distinguish pathway-specific signal use from correlated signal
use and operator artifacts. The protocol may extend to other
biomedical signal domains where clinically relevant input regions
can be defined a priori, though the current evidence comes from
five ECG diagnoses on two datasets.

I. INTRODUCTION
Deep learning classifiers for electrocardiogram (ECG) anal￾ysis now achieve high discrimination across a growing set of
cardiac conditions [1]–[4], aided by large public datasets such
as PTB-XL [5] and CODE-15% [6]. But strong discrimination
does not tell us whether a model relies on disease-relevant
signal regions—a gap that matters for clinical deployment
beyond benchmark performance. A 1AVB classifier might
depend on QRS morphology instead of PR-interval timing; an
AFIB classifier might use ventricular rate irregularity, atrial
waveform features, or unrelated shortcuts. Standard bench￾mark metrics cannot distinguish these cases. Moreover, exist￾ing explanation methods rarely test whether disease-relevant
regions dominate over matched controls, or whether pathway
dependence holds up under dataset shift—sensitivity is not
specificity, and explanation conclusions can be fragile under
distribution shift [7], [8].
We address these gaps with a model-agnostic, matched￾control perturbation audit protocol. For each diagnosis we pre￾specify an expected positive pathway (e.g., the PR segment
for 1AVB, the QRS complex for bundle branch block) and
compare targeted perturbations against anatomically adjacent
control regions that should matter less. A pathway claim is
accepted only if the target perturbation is more disruptive
than its strongest matched control—a stricter criterion than
perturbation sensitivity alone. We further evaluate pathway
specificity under frozen-weight transfer from CODE-15% to
cardiologist-validated PTB-XL fold 10, providing an external
check on whether explanation conclusions are dataset-specific.
The protocol is model-agnostic: the same perturbation design
applies to any classifier accepting 12-lead ECG input, and
the five diseases are a case-study panel chosen to span three
diagnostic pathway categories (timing, morphology, rhythm),
not an exhaustive clinical survey.

We instantiate the audit across four model architectures
(XGBoost, ResNet, SE-ResNet, and a lightweight Trans￾former) at three representation levels—simple summary fea￾tures, timing-enriched handcrafted features, and raw signal—
to assess whether pathway dependence is consistent across
architectures and levels of signal access. The protocol is
evaluated internally on CODE-15% (345,779 exams, patient￾level split) and externally on PTB-XL fold 10 (cardiologist￾validated labels).
Our primary contribution is the audit protocol itself—a
structured method for evaluating whether ECG classifiers base
decisions on disease-relevant signal regions, rather than on
correlated but clinically non-specific features. We show that
a matched-control design with external transfer can separate
pathway claims that remain anatomically specific and exter￾nally consistent from those that do not, and can identify cases
where target perturbation alone would produce misleading
conclusions. The protocol also reveals that the perturbation
operator itself is a critical methodological variable: zero￾masking, the most common occlusion method in the lit￾erature, creates hard-boundary artifacts that inflate control￾region disruption and can reverse specificity conclusions. A
continuity-preserving operator (linear interpolation) eliminates
this artifact and provides more conservative, anatomically
interpretable ASS estimates. The protocol thus addresses a
gap between standard discrimination benchmarks (which mea￾sure only predictive accuracy) and pathway-specific evidence
(which requires evidence about how models arrive at deci￾sions).
II. RELATED WORK
A. ECG Classification with Deep Learning
1D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and residual
architectures have become the dominant paradigm for auto￾mated ECG classification. Hannun et al. [1] demonstrated
cardiologist-level arrhythmia detection using a 34-layer 1D
CNN on ambulatory ECGs. On the PTB-XL benchmark,
Strodthoff et al. [2] established strong baselines with 1D
ResNets and fully convolutional networks across 71 diagnostic
classes; their follow-up review [3] confirmed that ResNet-style
architectures remain competitive against newer alternatives.
Mehari and Strodthoff [9] further advanced PTB-XL bench￾marks through self-supervised pre-training, while Chen et
al. [10] and Zubair et al. [11] contributed targeted architectures
for multi-class and imbalanced ECG classification.
Beyond vanilla ResNets, SE-ResNet [12] adds channel-wise
attention, and lightweight Transformer adaptations [13] have
been applied via patch-based self-attention. Recent hybrid
architectures combine these paradigms—Cardioformer [14]
couples multi-granularity patching with Transformer layers,
while xECGArch [15] separates morphology and rhythm pro￾cessing with dual CNNs. ECG-JEPA [16] pushed PTB-XL
performance to AUROC=0.945 through JEPA pre-training
on over one million records spanning ten datasets including
CODE-15%. Foundation models such as ECG-FM [17] fur￾ther scale pre-training, though their explanation behavior and
pathway-level auditability remain unexplored. Prior to the deep
learning era, classical machine learning methods—including
XGBoost, random forests, and support vector machines—
were widely applied to handcrafted ECG features and remain
competitive baselines on structured feature sets [18], [19].
Despite these advances across both classical and deep
learning paradigms, the common evaluation framework em￾phasizes discrimination metrics on held-out test splits. It
remains unclear whether these models base their decisions
on disease-relevant signal regions, and whether region-specific
dependence survives cross-dataset transfer. This gap motivates
our multi-level audit protocol, which applies identical pathway
questions across representation levels—from a feature-based
XGBoost baseline to a raw-signal ResNet—allowing us to
assess pathway dependence across both classical and deep
learning models.
B. Explainability and Perturbation Methods
Post-hoc explanation methods—including saliency maps,
occlusion-based sensitivity, guided backpropagation, and in￾tegrated gradients—have been systematically evaluated on
ECG tasks. Storas et al. [20] compared nine gradient-based ˚
methods on synthetic 12-lead ECGs and found that no single
method works best across all measurement tasks, with con￾siderable disagreement between human expert evaluation and
perturbation-based metrics. Suh et al. [21] evaluated eleven
attribution methods across five large ECG datasets and re￾ported that Guided Grad-CAM best aligned with cardiologists’
assessment while localization-based metrics better reflected
human judgment than perturbation-based ones. Plagwitz et
al. [22] assessed the reliability of feature attribution explana￾tions in ECG analysis through systematic perturbation testing,
reporting that explanation reliability varies substantially across
attribution methods and disease categories. Al-Zaiti et al. [23]
found that clinically deployed saliency maps for occlusion
MI detection were rated only slightly clinically relevant by
practicing clinicians, underscoring the gap between current
explanation quality and clinical expectations.
Perturbation-based evaluation—in which input regions are
removed or altered to measure prediction change—provides
a more direct test of feature dependence than gradient-based
attributions alone. Wagner et al. [24] proposed a structured
XAI framework for ECG that combines occlusion-based san￾ity checks, glocal attribution aggregation, and concept-based
analysis, providing quantitative evidence that model behav￾ior can align with cardiologists’ decision rules. Bender et
al. [25] demonstrated that a ResNet trained for 12-lead ECG
classification learns features analogous to clinical diagnostic
criteria including P-wave morphology, QRS duration, and
PR interval. Recent work has also applied wave masking
and reconstruction-based perturbation strategies [26], [27],
and Shapley-value-based ablation [28] to quantify localized
feature importance in ECG classifiers. Beyond ECG, Ross
et al. [29] demonstrated that constraining models to produce
“right” explanations during training can improve generaliza￾tion, providing an alternative to post-hoc auditing—though
their approach requires ground-truth explanation annotations
that are rarely available for clinical ECG tasks.

Despite these advances, three structural limitations persist
across the existing ECG explanation literature. First, existing
perturbation studies rarely incorporate matched anatomical
controls: they test whether a region matters, but not whether
disease-specific regions matter more than adjacent control
regions. This is the key distinction between perturbation
sensitivity (a region is important) and anatomical specificity (a
disease-specific region is more important than its anatomically
adjacent controls)—a distinction we operationalize through the
ASS metric and matched-control design. Second, explanation
conclusions are typically validated only within the training
distribution. Adebayo et al. [7] showed that saliency maps
can fail basic sanity checks under simple input transfor￾mations, Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola [30] demonstrated that
interpretability methods can be fragile under input pertur￾bations, and Ong Ly et al. [31] demonstrated that hidden
data acquisition biases in ECG datasets can inflate model
performance by up to 20%, with AUROC dropping from 0.90
to 0.70 under external validation. In medical imaging more
broadly, DeGrave et al. [32] showed that deep learning models
for radiographic COVID-19 detection selected clinically irrele￾vant shortcuts over meaningful signal—a finding that directly
parallels our concern about ECG classifiers exploiting non￾specific waveform features. Third, few studies test whether
explanation claims survive external dataset shift [8]. These
gaps directly motivate our matched-control perturbation design
with frozen-weight cross-dataset transfer.
C. Dataset Use and Cross-Dataset Validation
The two largest public 12-lead ECG datasets—PTB-XL [5]
(21,837 records, cardiologist-validated labels) and CODE-15%
[6] (345,779 exams, automated labels)—have enabled a wide
range of deep learning studies. PTB-XL provides carefully
annotated multi-label diagnoses with rich metadata including
signal quality indicators and demographic attributes, while
CODE-15% offers an order of magnitude more samples but
with labels derived from an automated interpretation system.
This label-source asymmetry introduces a critical distinction:
models trained on CODE-15% may learn to replicate the
automated labeling logic rather than physician-level diagnostic
features, creating a label circularity risk that varies by disease
category. The PTB-XL+ dataset [33] supplements PTB-XL
with 71 handcrafted features spanning heart rate variability,
QRS morphology, and signal quality metrics, enabling direct
comparisons between learned representations and classical
ECG parameters.
Cross-dataset validation remains underutilized in the ECG
deep learning literature, and where it has been attempted,
the results are sobering. Bickmann et al. [18] benchmarked
time-series versus feature-based methods on PTB-XL but
did not include external validation. Soltanieh et al. [34]
addressed out-of-distribution generalization for self-supervised
ECG representations, showing that dataset shift degrades stan￾dard supervised baselines. Frank et al. [35] reported that
models achieving AUROC>0.90 within-dataset for myocardial
ischemia detection experienced substantial performance drops
across six public ECG databases. At the foundation-model
scale, ECGFounder [36] and recent benchmarking efforts [37]
confirm that cross-domain generalization remains a key chal￾lenge even for large pre-trained models with diverse training
data.
The consistent picture is that external validation across
datasets with different label sources, populations, and acqui￾sition protocols is widely recommended but rarely executed,
and even less often applied to explanation claims. Our study
addresses this gap through frozen-weight transfer from CODE￾15% to cardiologist-validated PTB-XL fold 10, treating the
external dataset as a simultaneous check on both prediction
quality and pathway explanation consistency.
D. Clinical Pathway and Mechanistic Analysis
Clinical ECG interpretation relies on well-defined phys￾iological features: PR interval for atrioventricular conduc￾tion timing, QRS duration and morphology for ventricular
conduction, RR interval regularity for rhythm classification,
and P-wave morphology for atrial activity assessment [38].
These features define distinct diagnostic pathways for condi￾tions such as 1AVB (prolonged PR>200ms), bundle branch
blocks (wide QRS>120ms with characteristic terminal/lateral
R patterns), sinus bradycardia (low ventricular rate), and atrial
fibrillation (absent or fibrillatory atrial activity).
Recent studies have directly tested whether deep ECG
models learn these clinically meaningful features. Hempel et
al. [39] extended an XAI framework to match deep learning
relevances with PR interval and QRS duration from PTB-XL+,
reporting that 96.0% of high-confidence 1AVB predictions had
PR>200ms and 98.6% of high-confidence LBBB predictions
had QRS>120ms—strong evidence that the model internally
represents clinical thresholds. Riberg et al. [40] performed a
concordance analysis between ResNet predictions and cardi￾ology guideline thresholds, finding that RR interval features
dominated for sinus bradycardia and tachycardia while mor￾phological features showed weaker correlation. Hammer et
al. [41] introduced an architecture that explicitly separates
rhythm (long-term) and morphology (short-term) processing,
demonstrating that fused explanations correlate with clinical
diagnostic criteria. A systematic review by Ayano et al. [42]
confirmed that interpretable ML studies for ECG increasingly
target clinical parameters such as PR interval, QRS duration,
and RR variability.
Despite this progress, a critical gap remains: existing studies
confirm that models attend to clinically relevant features,
but they do not test whether a disease-specific signal region
dominates over anatomically adjacent controls, or whether
such pathway specificity survives dataset shift. Demonstrating
feature relevance is not the same as demonstrating feature
specificity. Our disease-centered, matched-control perturbation
audit addresses this gap: for five diagnoses spanning timing,
morphology, and rhythm pathways, we pre-specify expected
positive regions grounded in clinical physiology, compare
targeted perturbations against matched controls, and verify
pathway specificity under frozen-weight external transfer. This
design transforms clinical pathway knowledge into testable,
falsifiable audit criteria.

III. METHODS
A. Dataset
CODE-15%: Brazilian ECG dataset with 345,779 12-lead
exams (400Hz, 10-second duration) from 233,770 patients.
We use five target conditions because they span three distinct
diagnostic pathways: 1AVB (timing), CRBBB/CLBBB (mor￾phology), and SBRAD/AFIB (rhythm). Their prevalences are
1.65%, 2.80%, 1.74%, 1.62%, and 2.03%, respectively.
Label source and circularity risk: Labels were derived
from the CODE dataset’s automated ECG interpretation sys￾tem. CODE serves as an automated-label internal audit cohort.
The risk of label circularity—where the model reproduces the
automated labeling logic instead of recovering physician-level
diagnostic mechanisms—varies by disease:
• 1AVB—Highest risk: The label definition (PR>200ms)
and PR-interval proxy features overlap heavily, so models
may learn the automated threshold instead of clinical AV￾conduction features.
• SBRAD—High risk: Heart-rate-based rules
(HR<60bpm) directly overlap with the label source,
making learned rate-threshold behavior hard to
distinguish from label replication.
• CRBBB/CLBBB—Moderate risk: QRS morphology
criteria (width >120ms, terminal R′
/broad R patterns)
may align with the automated interpretation system’s
feature extraction.
• AFIB—Moderate risk: P-wave absence and atrial activ￾ity metrics may overlap with the rhythm classifier com￾ponent of the automated system, though RR irregularity
alone provides only a partial signal.
To buffer these risks, we treat PTB-XL fold 10 (cardiologist￾validated labels) as the primary external validation, and we
recommend interpreting internal CODE findings as evidence
about model behavior relative to the existing automated￾label system, not as evidence of physician-level diagnostic
reasoning.
Patient-level split: 60% train (207,232 samples), 20% vali￾dation (69,045 samples), 20% test (69,520 samples). Random
seed 42 for reproducibility. Patient-level splitting ensures no
patient appears in multiple splits, preventing leakage from
patient-specific patterns.
B. Disease-Centered Finding Map and Audit Panel
The audit framework is built around a compact, literature￾guided finding map covering five diagnoses: 1AVB, CRBBB,
CLBBB, SBRAD, and AFIB. For each disease we pre-specify
(i) the expected positive pathway, (ii) matched negative/control
regions that should produce smaller effects, and (iii) any
ambiguous pathway treated as hypothesis-testing. The map is
intentionally compact and disease-centered.
SBRAD now contributes matched pathway audits on both
CODE and PTB-XL via rate normalization with QRS and ST
controls, so it enters pathway-score aggregation as a narrower
cross-dataset audit case. AFIB is handled differently from the
outset: RR irregularity alone is an explicit ambiguity test.
Clinical anchoring. Each target region and control pairing
is grounded in established ECG diagnostic criteria [38]. The
target window maps to the clinically accepted diagnostic
feature for that disease (PR prolongation for 1AVB, QRS
widening for BBB, low ventricular rate for SBRAD, absent
P-waves for AFIB). Each matched control is anatomically
adjacent to the target and involves a physiologically distinct
structure (e.g., ST segment vs PR interval, QRS complex vs
atrial window), ensuring that the control perturbation tests
a plausible alternative signal channel rather than a trivially
irrelevant region. This design ensures that a positive ASS
reflects genuine anatomical specificity: the target pathway is
more important than its most disruptive anatomically adjacent
alternative.
C. The Audit Protocol as a Model-Agnostic Method
The audit protocol is designed to be model-agnostic:
the same perturbation windows, matched-control compar￾isons, and evaluation metrics apply to any classifier that
accepts 12-lead ECG input, regardless of architecture (con￾volutional, transformer-based, tree-based, or hybrid). The five
diagnoses—1AVB, CRBBB, CLBBB, SBRAD, and AFIB—
serve as a case-study panel chosen to span three clinically
distinct diagnostic pathway categories (timing, morphology,
rhythm), and are not intended as an exhaustive clinical survey.
The protocol itself does not depend on the specific diseases,
the model architecture, or the training dataset. We demon￾strate this model-agnostic property by instantiating the audit
across four architectures (XGBoost, ResNet, SE-ResNet, and a
lightweight Transformer) and three representation levels, with
external validation on an independent cardiologist-validated
dataset.
D. Supporting Models and Representation Ladder
We use three representations to support the audit protocol:
(i) simple summary features, (ii) timing-enriched handcrafted
features, and (iii) raw-signal deep learning. Together they span
the range from minimal to full signal access. Secondary archi￾tectures (SE-ResNet and a lightweight Transformer) provide
context for how sensitive the audit conclusions are to model
choice [12], [13].
E. Supporting Feature-Space Baseline: XGBoost + Simple
Summary Features (98D)
Feature extraction (98 dimensions):
• Rhythm features (14): RR intervals
(Mean/Std/Min/Max/Median/Range), HR (Mean/Std),
HRV (RMSSD/SDNN/pNN50/CV), RR Irregularity,
QRS Count
• Amplitude features (84): Per-lead statistics
(Mean/Std/Min/Max/Range/RMS/PeakToPeak) for
12 leads
No demographic or site metadata were included in this feature
set.
Role in the study: This is the lowest-access baseline. It tests
how far rhythm and coarse amplitude summaries can go before
explicit timing or raw waveform detail becomes necessary.

G. Supporting Raw-Signal Model: 1D ResNet
Architecture:
• Input: Raw 12-lead ECG (12 × 4096), z-score normal￾ized per lead
• Preprocessing: Original signals (4000 samples at 400Hz,
10s duration) were resampled to 4096 samples via linear
interpolation, extending the temporal window to 10.24s.
This preserves the full 10s recording while providing a
power-of-two input length compatible with 4× downsam￾pling stages.
• Backbone: 4 ResNet stages with residual blocks:
– Stage 1: 2 blocks, 64 channels, kernel=7, stride=2
– Stage 2: 2 blocks, 128 channels, kernel=7, stride=2
– Stage 3: 2 blocks, 256 channels, kernel=7, stride=2
– Stage 4: 2 blocks, 512 channels, kernel=7, stride=2
• Residual block: Conv1D → BatchNorm → ReLU →
Conv1D → BatchNorm → skip connection → ReLU
• Pooling: AdaptiveAvgPool1D(1) → flatten to 512-dim
vector
• Classifier: Dropout(0.2) → Linear(512 → 5) → Sigmoid
• Loss: BCEWithLogitsLoss with per-class weights (in￾verse prevalence)
• Parameters: 1.2M trainable parameters
• Complexity: 0.8 GFLOPs per sample
Training: Adam optimizer (lr=0.001), ReduceLROn￾Plateau scheduler (factor=0.5, patience=5), early stopping
(patience=10 on validation loss), batch size 64, trained for
up to 50 epochs (early stopping typically triggered at epoch
23–28). Training time: 2.5 hours on A100 GPU (single run).
Multi-seed training: To assess statistical robustness, we
trained 4 independent ResNet runs: 3 with different model
initialization seeds (42, 123, 456) on the primary patient
split (seed=42), and 1 on a second independent patient split
(seed=123) with model seed 42. All other hyperparameters
were identical. This lets us estimate both within-split variance

I. Predefined Perturbation Operator
We used linear interpolation as the predefined perturbation
operator for all target and matched-control windows. For each
perturbed window, the original signal segment was replaced by
a straight-line interpolation between the two boundary values,
preserving local waveform continuity and avoiding the hard
discontinuities introduced by zero-masking [45]. ECG signals
reflect continuous physiological processes where abrupt sig￾nal discontinuities are not expected [46], and perturbation￾based explanation is an established paradigm in ECG inter￾pretability [47]. This operator is simple, deterministic, and
applies identically to target and control windows. We do
not assume that linear interpolation generates physiologically
perfect counterfactual ECGs; therefore, all pathway-specific
conclusions in this study should be interpreted conditionally on
this predefined continuity-preserving operator. A preregistered
comparison of three perturbation operators (zero-masking,
linear interpolation, beat-conditioned inpainting) across two
disease-pathway pairs, two architectures, dose-response, and
lead-local dimensions is provided in the Supplementary Ma￾terial (8-run summary table, full preregistration block).

A preregistered comparison of three perturbation operators

F. Confirmatory Inference: Clustered Bootstrap and Multiplic￾ity Control
The primary external audit tests 15 pre-specified hypotheses
of the form H0 : ASS ≤ 0 (one-sided) under the primary
linear-interpolation operator on PTB-XL fold 10. To address
within-patient correlation and multiplicity, we apply two com￾plementary safeguards.
Patient-clustered bootstrap. All confidence intervals and
Pr(ASS> 0) values are computed via patient-level cluster
bootstrap (1,000 replicates, seed 42). In each replicate, patients
(not individual ECGs) are resampled with replacement; all
ECGs belonging to a resampled patient are included, preserv￾ing the within-patient correlation structure. ASS is computed
on the paired target-versus-control perturbation effects within
each replicate, maintaining the matched-subject design. The
reported Pr(ASS> 0) is the fraction of bootstrap replicates in
which the replicate ASS exceeds zero, providing a bootstrap￾based one-sided p-value for H0 : ASS ≤ 0.
Multiplicity control. The 15 external tests constitute a
single confirmatory family. We apply the Benjamini–Hochberg
false discovery rate (BH-FDR) procedure at α = 0.05 to
control the expected proportion of false positives among
rejected hypotheses. Table XII reports the bootstrap p-values,
BH-FDR thresholds, and Storey q-values for all 15 pairs.
Impact on tier assignments. Under BH-FDR at α = 0.05,

B. Why Discrimination Metrics Alone Are Insufficient
A central claim of this paper is that standard discrimination
metrics—F1, AUROC, AUPRC—are necessary but insufficient

signal pathways under this audit. The audit results provide
specific evidence for this claim.

D. Relationship to Prior Work
Most prior ECG explanation studies use saliency maps or
single-region perturbation to show that specific signal regions
influence predictions [7], [20], [21]. Recent work has pro￾posed explanation frameworks for ECG with varying levels
of clinical grounding [3], [24]. The present study differs in
two respects. First, we require target-region perturbations to
be compared against anatomically matched controls—a stricter
criterion that can reveal false-positive pathway claims, as
the 1AVB case demonstrates. Second, we evaluate whether
pathway specificity persists under frozen-weight transfer to
an independent dataset, addressing the concern that explana￾tion conclusions may be dataset-specific [8], [31]. The audit
protocol is thus an explanation evaluation method, not an
explanation generation method.
E. Methodological Implications
The protocol is model-agnostic by design. It can be
applied to any classifier that accepts 12-lead ECG input—we
demonstrated it across four architectures (XGBoost, ResNet,
SE-ResNet, Transformer) at three representation levels. Apply￾ing the protocol to different architectures revealed that path￾way behavior can vary across models even when trained on
identical data: the Transformer’s architecture-specific rhythm
weakness and XGBoost’s complementary AFIB feature use
are findings that depend on having the protocol instantiated on
those models. A single-architecture application of the protocol
to ResNet would still produce valid per-model conclusions
(e.g., CLBBB pathway-supported, 1AVB not supported). The
cross-architecture demonstration confirms that the protocol
does not tie its conclusions to a specific model class.
Matched controls are not optional. The 1AVB case
demonstrates that large target-pathway effects can coexist with
even larger non-target dependence. Without matched controls,
1AVB would have been misclassified as a timing-specific
success. Every pathway claim in the audit protocol must
survive a matched-control specificity comparison, and the ASS
metric operationalizes this requirement directly.
External transfer separates stable from unstable path￾way claims. The protocol’s second key design element—
frozen-weight transfer to an independent, cardiologist￾validated dataset—acts as a stress test for pathway specificity.
CRBBB and CLBBB survive this test on all three architec￾tures under the primary operator (PTB-XL ASS positive with
CI> 0, CDDC= 1.0 for all 6 model-disease pairs). This is
the protocol’s central positive finding: QRS-morphology path￾way specificity is architecture-invariant and dataset-invariant.
1AVB external transfer confirms negative ASS on all three ar￾chitectures, corroborating the matched-control reversal. AFIB
external transfer reveals the zero-masking positive as operator
artifact—ASS is negative on both datasets under the primary
operator. The combination of external transfer and operator
selection prevents both classes of false-positive conclusion:
without external transfer, SBRAD-ResNet’s internal positive
would stand alone without external confirmation of direction
under dataset shift; without operator selection, AFIB would
appear cross-dataset positive.
Interpretation boundaries. To clarify what the current
audit design can and cannot support, we distinguish four levels
of evidence:
1) Pathway sensitivity: Perturbation of the target region
causes a performance drop.
2) Pathway specificity: The target-region drop exceeds the
drop from matched control perturbations (ASS> 0).
3) Mechanistic validity: The model uses the same physi￾ological mechanisms that clinicians employ.
4) Clinical validity: The mechanism holds under physician
annotation or predicts real clinical outcomes.
The audit conclusions in this paper are structured around
pathway sensitivity and specificity (levels 1–2). Claims about
mechanistic or clinical validity (levels 3–4) require additional
evidence—clinician review of failure cases, formal mediation
analysis, or prospective validation—that is beyond the scope of
this study. This audit supports evidence plausibility under a
controlled perturbation protocol, not mechanistic causality
or clinical utility. Pathway-supported designations indicate
that a model’s predictions are more sensitive to disease￾relevant than to control-region perturbation under a primary
operator; they do not certify that the model uses the same
physiological mechanisms as a clinician, nor that the model is
safe for deployment.
Patient-level splitting, multi-seed training, and compre￾hensive metrics are essential protocol-level practices that
prevent data leakage, confirm training stability (within-split
SD= 0.0025), and capture the full performance picture beyond
a single metric. The representation ladder confirms that feature
complementarity operates across three axes (rhythm, morphol￾ogy, timing), and that explicit proxy features can recover
clinically relevant signal without end-to-end learning.

Several directions merit further investigation. The cross￾architecture perturbation audit (Section IV-C) has been com￾pleted on CODE-15%; extending it to the external PTB￾XL dataset under linear interpolation would reveal whether

VI. CONCLUSION
We propose a model-agnostic matched-control pathway au￾dit protocol for evaluating pathway-specific evidence in ECG
classifiers. The protocol requires that (i) targeted perturba￾tions are compared against anatomically matched controls,
(ii) the perturbation operator is documented and compared
via a preregistered operator-comparison battery, (iii) path￾way specificity is re-tested under frozen-weight transfer to
an independent cardiologist-validated dataset, and (iv) per￾model evidence tiers—pathway-supported, evidence-limited,
not supported—are assigned to each (architecture, disease)
pair, constraining interpretation under operator dependence
and external transfer without aggregating across architectures.
Applied to five diagnoses as a case-study panel, the protocol
reveals heterogeneity invisible to discrimination metrics alone:
1AVB is Not supported across all three architectures on
both datasets—a replicated matched-control failure demon￾strating that target-only perturbation can produce false-positive
pathway claims; CRBBB and CLBBB both reach Pathway￾supported on all three architectures (internal+external positive
ASS with CI> 0 on both datasets, CDDC= 1.0 for all
6 pairs), confirming that QRS-morphology pathway speci￾ficity is architecture-invariant and dataset-invariant; SBRAD
splits—ResNet Evidence-limited (rate-pathway positive inter￾nally and externally but external CI narrowly crosses zero),
SE-ResNet and Transformer Not supported—demonstrating
that rate-pathway learning is architecture-dependent; AFIB is
Not supported on all three architectures on both datasets, with
its earlier zero-masking positive revealed as operator artifact.
Overall, 6 of 15 model-disease pairs reach Pathway-supported,
1 is Evidence-limited, and 8 are Not supported. The sole
Evidence-limited designation (SBRAD-ResNet) reflects nar￾row CI margin, not absent external data or protocol failure. A
preregistered operator-comparison battery shows that operator
choice strongly influences pathway conclusions: zero-masking
creates boundary artifacts that can reverse specificity, while
linear interpolation provides more interpretable behavior. The
CRBBB case is instructive: zero-masking produced the appear￾ance of external pathway failure (PTB-XL ASS−0.023Z
), but
the primary operator reveals robust external pathway speci￾ficity (ASS 0.455L
)—demonstrating that operator selection
is a necessary precondition for pathway-specificity claims.
Standard discrimination metrics (AUROC> 0.98 for all five
diseases) are insufficient for evaluating whether a classifier
uses disease-consistent signal pathways under this audit. The
matched-control audit principle, combined with operator se￾lection and external transfer, may extend to other biomedical
signal domains where clinically relevant input regions can be
defined a priori, though the current evidence is limited to five
ECG diagnoses on two datasets.

JBHI 更适合改成**“问题驱动型叙事”**：不是按你做实验的顺序写，而是按审稿人需要相信的几个命题来组织。

你的论文核心其实不是“我们做了很多实验”，而是：

> 高 AUROC 不等于模型用了正确 ECG 通路；必须用 matched-control + operator control + external transfer 来审计 pathway-specific evidence。

所以大纲应该围绕这个核心重排。

# 建议的新大纲：压缩版 JBHI 主文结构

## Title

**Beyond Discrimination: Matched-Control Pathway Auditing for ECG Classifiers**

标题可以更短一点。现在标题没问题，但略长。

---

## Abstract

结构建议：

1. **Problem**：ECG classifiers can be accurate but may rely on non-specific signal regions.
2. **Method**：We propose a matched-control perturbation audit with predefined disease pathways, anatomical controls, operator documentation, and external transfer.
3. **Key results**：
   - 1AVB: target PR perturbation large, but QRS control stronger → false-positive pathway claim avoided.
   - BBB: QRS pathway supported across architectures and external dataset.
   - AFIB: zero-masking positive disappears under linear interpolation → operator artifact.
   - SBRAD: architecture-dependent.
4. **Conclusion**：Discrimination metrics are insufficient; pathway-specific evidence requires matched controls and operator-aware validation.

你现在 Abstract 信息量太大，尤其结果部分塞了太多数字。保留 4 个结论就够了。当前摘要已经把 1AVB、BBB、SBRAD、AFIB 全塞进去了，读起来像 Results 压缩包。fileciteturn0file0

# I. Introduction

目标：**2 页以内**。

## A. Motivation: High discrimination is not pathway evidence

写清楚：

- ECG deep models AUROC 很高。
- 但高 AUROC 不说明模型用的是临床一致区域。
- 例如 1AVB 可能不是靠 PR，而是靠 QRS 或其他 shortcut。

## B. Gap: Existing XAI lacks specificity tests

不要展开成大综述，只讲三个 gap：

1. target-only perturbation 只能证明 sensitivity，不能证明 specificity；
2. 很少使用 anatomically matched controls；
3. 很少验证解释结论是否 survives dataset shift 和 perturbation operator change。

## C. Contribution

建议列 4 条：

1. 提出 matched-control pathway audit；
2. 定义 ASS / CDDC / evidence tiers；
3. 引入 operator-aware protocol，避免 zero-masking artifact；
4. 在五个 ECG diagnosis、三种 raw-signal architectures、两个 datasets 上验证。

这里不要再提前讲太多具体结果。

---

# II. Related Work

目标：**1 页左右**，甚至可以并入 Introduction 末尾。

建议只保留三个小段，不要四个大节。

## A. ECG explanation and perturbation methods

只服务于一句话：已有方法通常评估“哪个区域重要”，但很少评估“目标区域是否比 matched control 更重要”。

## B. Cross-dataset validation and shortcut learning

只服务于一句话：解释结论也会受 dataset shift 影响，所以需要 external transfer。

## C. Clinical pathway priors in ECG

只服务于一句话：ECG 的 PR/QRS/RR/atrial activity 可以被预定义成 audit target，使 pathway audit 可操作。

你现在 Related Work 从 ECG classification 讲到 foundation model，太像综述了。对于这篇论文，**ECG classification benchmark 不是主贡献背景，应该大幅压缩**。

---

# III. Methods

目标：**3 页左右**。

Methods 不要按“我们训练了哪些模型”的线性顺序写，而要按 audit protocol 写。

---

## A. Study Design Overview

先给审稿人一个总图：

- datasets：CODE-15% internal，PTB-XL fold 10 external；
- diseases：1AVB, CRBBB, CLBBB, SBRAD, AFIB；
- models：ResNet, SE-ResNet, Transformer；XGBoost as supporting feature-space baseline；
- core audit：target perturbation vs strongest matched control；
- external audit：frozen-weight transfer；
- evidence tier：Pathway-supported / Evidence-limited / Not supported。

这一节对应你现在 Fig. 1，但图必须重画。现在 Fig. 1 里有“figure retained / earlier zero-masking analysis”这种补丁式说明，很不适合主文。fileciteturn0file0

---

## B. Disease-Centered Pathway Map

保留你现在 Table I，但正文压缩。

表格内容很好，是论文最清楚的部分之一：  
1AVB 对 PR，BBB 对 QRS，SBRAD 对 rate，AFIB 对 atrial activity，同时列 matched controls。fileciteturn0file0

这部分只需要解释：

- target pathway 是 clinical prior；
- matched controls 是 anatomical / functional alternatives；
- audit 不是证明机制因果，而是检验 target 是否比 control 更特异。

---

## C. Models and Datasets

这里要极度压缩。

建议写成：

- CODE-15%：training/internal audit dataset；
- PTB-XL fold 10：external cardiologist-validated audit dataset；
- raw-signal models：ResNet, SE-ResNet, Transformer；
- XGBoost：supporting feature-space comparison，不进入 main tiering。

不要在正文展开每个模型的层数、kernel size、训练 epoch、batch size。这些全部放 Supplement。

主文只保留一个简表：

| Component | Role |
|---|---|
| ResNet | primary raw-signal audit model |
| SE-ResNet | channel-attention robustness check |
| Transformer | architecture contrast |
| XGBoost | feature-space support, not tiered |

---

## D. Matched-Control Perturbation Audit

这是 Methods 的核心。

写清楚三个东西：

### 1. Target perturbation

每个 disease perturb 哪个区域。

### 2. Matched controls

每个 target 对应哪些 control。

### 3. Primary operator

线性插值作为 primary operator。  
zero-masking / beat-inpainting 只作为 operator-sensitivity analysis，放 Supplement。

这里要注意：**不要在正文里不断为 linear interpolation 辩护**。一句话即可：

> Linear interpolation was predefined as the primary operator because it preserves local continuity and avoids hard-boundary artifacts.

---

## E. Audit Metrics and Evidence Tiers

保留：

\[
ASS = \Delta AUROC_{target} - \max_c \Delta AUROC_c
\]

解释：

- ASS > 0：target 比所有 controls 更 disruptive；
- ASS ≤ 0：不支持 pathway-specific claim；
- CDDC：internal/external direction 是否一致；
- tiering rules。

这一节应该很精炼。你现在这部分写得比较多，但本质很好，可以保留，只是压缩。

---

## F. Statistical Analysis

只保留：

- patient-level bootstrap CI；
- one-sided external ASS tests；
- BH-FDR across 15 tests；
- performance metrics are contextual, not primary evidence。

DeLong、permutation test、multi-seed、feature ablation 的细节都进 Supplement。

---

# IV. Results

Results 建议完全重排。不要按实验顺序，而是按“审稿人需要被说服的命题”组织。

---

## A. High Discrimination Does Not Resolve Pathway Evidence

目的：先建立矛盾。

内容：

- raw-signal models 在五个疾病上 AUROC 很高；
- 但这只是 classification context；
- 因此需要 audit。

这里只放一个小表即可：每个模型 overall/per-disease AUROC 或 F1，不要放太多指标。

你现在 Table III、Table IV、Fig. 2 可以压成一个简表或一个小图。ResNet 全疾病 AUROC > 0.98 是这个小节的核心，不需要列 Sens/Spec/PPV/NPV。fileciteturn0file0

---

## B. Target-Only Perturbation Can Produce False Pathway Claims: 1AVB

这是第一个核心结果，也应该是 Results 的“故事钩子”。

写法：

1. PR perturbation causes large AUROC drop；
2. target-only explanation would conclude PR dependence；
3. matched QRS control is even stronger；
4. therefore PR sensitivity ≠ PR specificity；
5. external PTB-XL replicates this failure；
6. all three architectures are Not supported。

这一节是你论文最有说服力的部分。现在内容很多，但其实可以压成一个图 + 一个段落。

建议图：  
**1AVB target vs controls bar plot**，显示 PR、QRS、ST、random 的 ΔAUROC。

---

## C. Matched-Control Audit Identifies Robust Positive Pathways: BBB

第二个核心结果：不是所有东西都被否定，protocol 能识别 positive evidence。

写法：

- CRBBB/CLBBB under linear interpolation；
- QRS target dominates controls；
- internal and external both positive；
- all three architectures Pathway-supported；
- CDDC = 1.0。

这里不要再分 CRBBB 和 CLBBB 写太久。它们可以合并成 **BBB morphology pathways**。

建议表：  
只放 ASS internal/external across architectures。

---

## D. Operator Choice Changes the Claim: AFIB

第三个核心结果：operator sensitivity。

写法：

1. zero-masking once suggested AFIB atrial pathway support；
2. primary linear interpolation makes ASS negative across architectures and datasets；
3. therefore earlier positive was operator artifact；
4. RR regularization also fails to provide pathway-specific AFIB support。

这节不用展开太多 feature-space XGBoost。XGBoost AFIB feature importance 可以放 Supplement，正文一句 “supporting feature-space analysis showed model-class heterogeneity” 即可。

---

## E. Architecture-Dependent Evidence: SBRAD

第四个核心结果：pathway evidence 是 model-specific。

写法：

- ResNet SBRAD rate pathway internal positive；
- external direction positive but CI crosses zero → Evidence-limited；
- SE-ResNet / Transformer Not supported；
- 说明 rate-pathway learning is architecture-dependent。

这节可以很短。SBRAD 不是主故事，不要让它占太多篇幅。

---

## F. Per-Model Audit Summary and Multiplicity Control

最后用总表收束。

这里放你的 Table X 的精简版，这是全文最重要的表。  
当前 Table X 结构是好的，但可以更紧凑。它直接显示 15 个 model-disease pair：6 Pathway-supported，1 Evidence-limited，8 Not supported。fileciteturn0file0

建议总表结构：

| Disease pathway | ResNet | SE-ResNet | Transformer | Main interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1AVB / PR | NS | NS | NS | PR sensitivity but no specificity |
| CRBBB / QRS | PS | PS | PS | robust QRS specificity |
| CLBBB / QRS | PS | PS | PS | robust QRS specificity |
| SBRAD / Rate | EL | NS | NS | architecture-dependent |
| AFIB / Atrial | NS | NS | NS | operator artifact / no specificity |

ASS 数值可以放在括号里，完整 CI 放 Supplement。

BH-FDR 结果用一句话：

> The six BBB pathway-supported pairs survived BH-FDR; SBRAD-ResNet did not, consistent with Evidence-limited.

不用把 Table XII 全放主文，除非版面允许。

---

# V. Discussion

Discussion 不要再按 disease 复述。按“意义”写。

---

## A. Discrimination Is Necessary but Not Sufficient

讲：AUROC > 0.98 仍然可能 Not supported。

用 1AVB/AFIB 作为例子。

---

## B. Matched Controls Are the Core Safeguard

讲：target-only perturbation 会产生 false-positive pathway claims。  
1AVB 是主例子。

---

## C. Operator Choice Is Part of the Explanation Claim

讲：zero-masking 不是中性操作，会制造 boundary artifacts。  
AFIB 和 CRBBB 是例子。

---

## D. Pathway Evidence Is Model-Specific

讲：不要从一个 architecture 推广到所有模型。  
SBRAD 是例子。

---

## E. Clinical and Methodological Boundaries

讲清楚：

- audit 支持 pathway specificity，不等于 clinical mechanism；
- 不证明医生级机制；
- 不证明部署安全；
- 只是在 predefined pathway + perturbation protocol 下做证据分层。

---

# VI. Limitations

目标：半页到一页。

你现在 limitations 太长，有 12 条，很多像补充说明。建议压成 5 条：

1. only two datasets, one external dataset；
2. CODE labels are automated；
3. perturbation operators are imperfect counterfactuals；
4. only five ECG diagnoses；
5. no clinician review / subgroup fairness / prospective validation。

不要把所有未来能做的事情都列进去。审稿人不是要看你自我否定 12 条。

---

# VII. Conclusion

目标：一段，最多两段。

建议结论：

> We introduced a matched-control pathway audit for ECG classifiers. Across five diagnoses, high discrimination did not guarantee pathway-specific evidence. BBB QRS pathways were robustly supported, 1AVB and AFIB were not supported despite plausible target sensitivity, and SBRAD was architecture-dependent. These findings show that pathway claims require matched controls, operator-aware perturbation, and external transfer, not target-only perturbation or AUROC alone.

---

# Supplementary Material 结构

你现在很多内容不是不要，而是应该放 Supplement。

建议 Supplement 按这个结构：

## S1. Dataset preprocessing and label mapping  
## S2. Model architectures and hyperparameters  
## S3. Feature extraction details  
## S4. Full classification performance  
## S5. Full perturbation protocols  
## S6. Operator-comparison battery  
## S7. Cross-architecture detailed ASS/PSS tables  
## S8. External transfer details  
## S9. Statistical testing and BH-FDR  
## S10. Additional diagnostics: AFIB and SBRAD  

这样主文就会清爽很多。

---

# 最推荐的 Results 叙事顺序

你现在 Results 是“实验顺序”：

> 分类性能 → 1AVB → QRS/RR/AFIB → 跨架构 → 外部验证 → 总结 → 统计

我建议改成“论证顺序”：

> **高 AUROC 不够 → 1AVB 证明 target-only 会错 → BBB 证明 protocol 能找到真阳性 → AFIB 证明 operator 会制造假阳性 → SBRAD 证明 pathway evidence 是模型特异的 → 总表收束**

这个顺序更像一篇 JBHI 方法论文。

---

# 一句话判断

你不是实验太多，而是**把实验日志写成了论文主线**。  
应该改成：**一个 protocol，四个证据场景，一个总表收束。**

最理想的主文故事是：

1. **Why audit?** 高 AUROC 不够。  
2. **Why matched controls?** 1AVB 会反转。  
3. **Does audit find positives?** BBB 稳定支持。  
4. **Why operator-aware?** AFIB zero-masking 是 artifact。  
5. **Why per-model?** SBRAD architecture-dependent。  
6. **Final evidence tier:** 6 PS / 1 EL / 8 NS。

对，你这个判断是对的。

**“Discrimination Is Necessary but Not Sufficient” 不适合作为 Discussion 的一个并列小节**，因为它其实是整篇论文的总论点。后面的 matched controls、operator choice、external transfer、per-model tiering，都是在解释“为什么 AUROC 不够”。

所以 Discussion 可以进一步压缩成一个更强的结构：**先总起一句，然后只保留 3 个真正有增量的小节**。

---

# 建议改成这个 Discussion 结构

## V. Discussion

### Opening paragraph：总起，不单独成节

开头直接用一段话概括：

> This study shows that high discrimination does not imply pathway-specific evidence. Across five ECG diagnoses, all models achieved strong classification performance, yet the matched-control audit separated robust pathway support from target sensitivity, operator artifacts, and architecture-dependent evidence. The central implication is that pathway claims require specificity tests, not only performance metrics or target-region perturbation.

这一段就承担你原来 **A. Discrimination Is Necessary but Not Sufficient** 的作用。  
不要单独设小节，否则后面会变成重复解释。

---

## A. Matched Controls Convert Sensitivity Into Specificity

这一节讲 1AVB。

核心观点：

- target perturbation 只能证明“这个区域有用”；
- matched-control 才能证明“这个区域比合理对照更特异”；
- 1AVB 是关键例子：PR perturbation 很大，但 QRS control 更大；
- 所以 target-only perturbation 会产生 false-positive pathway claim。

这一节可以写成 **1–2 段**，不要再复述所有数字。

建议表达：

> The 1AVB case illustrates why matched controls are not a technical refinement but a requirement for pathway claims. PR-window perturbation produced a large and clinically plausible degradation, which would usually be interpreted as evidence that the model uses AV-conduction timing. However, the matched QRS control was more disruptive under the primary operator and on the external dataset. Thus, the model was PR-sensitive but not PR-specific. This distinction is exactly what standard perturbation explanations miss.

---

## B. Operator Choice Is Part of the Claim

这一节讲 AFIB，也可以顺带提 CRBBB。

核心观点：

- perturbation operator 不是中性工具；
- zero-masking 会引入 hard-boundary artifact；
- AFIB under zero-masking 看起来 positive，但 linear interpolation 下消失；
- CRBBB under zero-masking 甚至会造成 external failure 假象；
- 所以 pathway claim 必须说明 operator，并最好做 operator sensitivity。

建议表达：

> The audit also shows that perturbation operators can determine the direction of a pathway conclusion. AFIB appeared to have cross-dataset atrial-window support under zero-masking, but this signal disappeared under the continuity-preserving primary operator. Conversely, CRBBB looked transfer-stressed under zero-masking but became robustly pathway-supported under linear interpolation. These reversals show that the perturbation operator is part of the explanation claim, not a secondary implementation detail.

这一节不要展开“linear interpolation 为什么最好”，因为 Methods 已经说过。Discussion 只讲意义。

---

## C. Pathway Evidence Should Be Assigned Per Model

这一节讲 BBB 和 SBRAD。

核心观点：

- BBB 是强阳性：三种 architecture 都 supported；
- SBRAD 是模型依赖：ResNet EL，SE-ResNet / Transformer NS；
- 所以不要把一个 architecture 的解释结论泛化为 disease-level claim；
- evidence tier 应该 per architecture-disease pair。

建议表达：

> The cross-architecture audit suggests that pathway evidence should be assigned to models, not diseases in the abstract. QRS-morphology evidence for CRBBB and CLBBB was stable across ResNet, SE-ResNet, and Transformer, making it the strongest positive finding in the study. In contrast, SBRAD rate-pathway evidence was architecture-dependent: ResNet showed directionally replicated but statistically limited support, whereas SE-ResNet and Transformer were not supported. This heterogeneity argues against reporting a single disease-level explanation without specifying the audited model.

---

## D. Scope and Limitations

把原来的 limitations 合并进 Discussion 最后一个小节，别再单独写很长。

保留 4–5 个限制：

- 只有两个数据集，一个外部验证集；
- CODE labels 是 automated labels；
- perturbation 不是完美 physiological counterfactual；
- 只覆盖五个 ECG diagnoses；
- 没有 clinician review / prospective validation。

建议表达：

> Several boundaries are important. First, the audit evaluates pathway specificity under predefined perturbation operators; it does not prove mechanistic equivalence to clinician reasoning. Second, CODE-15% labels are automated, and PTB-XL fold 10 only partly buffers label-circularity concerns. Third, linear interpolation is more conservative than zero-masking but remains an imperfect physiological counterfactual. Finally, the audit covers five diagnoses and three raw-signal architectures; broader disease panels, additional external datasets, clinician review, and subgroup analyses are needed before drawing clinical deployment conclusions.

---

# 压缩后的 Discussion 大纲

最终建议就是：

## V. Discussion

**总起段：High discrimination does not imply pathway-specific evidence.**

### A. Matched Controls Convert Sensitivity Into Specificity  
主讲 1AVB。

### B. Operator Choice Is Part of the Claim  
主讲 AFIB，顺带 CRBBB。

### C. Pathway Evidence Should Be Assigned Per Model  
主讲 BBB positive 和 SBRAD heterogeneity。

### D. Scope and Limitations  
讲边界，不自我重复。

---

# 不建议保留的 Discussion 小节

我不建议保留这些独立小节：

| 原小节 | 问题 |
|---|---|
| Discrimination Is Necessary but Not Sufficient | 这是总论点，不是并列讨论点 |
| The Limits of Post-Hoc Explainability | 和 matched controls 高度重复 |
| Relationship to Prior Work | 可以并入 Introduction / Related Work，不必 Discussion 单独讲 |
| Methodological Implications | 内容会和 A/B/C 重复 |
| Future Work | 可以并入 Limitations 最后一两句 |
| Long limitations list | 会显得论文问题太多，而且占页数 |

---

# 更狠的版本

Discussion 可以只保留 **4 个自然段**，不设太多小标题：

1. 总结核心发现：AUROC 不等于 pathway evidence。
2. 1AVB：matched controls 的必要性。
3. AFIB/CRBBB：operator choice 的重要性。
4. BBB/SBRAD + limitations：per-model evidence 和边界。

如果你要冲 JBHI 页数，我更推荐这种短 Discussion。你现在论文最大的问题不是讨论不够，而是**解释太多次同一个主张**。Discussion 应该收束，而不是重新展开。

**按 JBHI 以前公开说明/编辑部回复：Supplement 如果放在同一个 manuscript PDF 末尾，是算入页数的。** 也就是说，不是你写个 “Supplementary Material” 标题就自动不算。公开讨论中引用的 JBHI 规则写法是：regular paper 页数上限 12 页，且 **including supplementary material**；编辑部回复也说 supplementary material added at the end of manuscript is included in the page limit. citeturn347390search2

但这里有一个关键区别：

**1. Main manuscript 里的 Appendix / Supplement：算页数。**  
你现在这个 PDF 第 23–30 页的 Appendix 和 Supplementary Material 是跟正文、参考文献放在同一个主 PDF 里的，所以大概率会被当作 manuscript pages。你这篇当前是 30 页，不能靠“这几页叫 Supplement”来规避。fileciteturn0file0

**2. 作为独立 supplementary file 上传：通常不按主文页数计算，但要看 ScholarOne/投稿系统和当期要求。**  
很多 IEEE 期刊允许把 supplementary material 作为 separate supporting document 上传，供审稿使用或线上发布。但 JBHI 对“页数限制”的措辞比较严格，所以最稳妥的做法是：**主 manuscript PDF 控制在 12 页以内，Supplement 单独上传，不放在主 PDF 末尾。**

所以你的处理策略应该是：

**主文 PDF：** 只保留 title / abstract / main text / key figures / key tables / references，目标 10–12 页。  
**Supplementary PDF：** 单独文件，放 hyperparameters、完整表格、operator-comparison battery、multi-seed、SBRAD diagnostic、AFIB method-comparison、reproducibility details。

你这篇现在最危险的不是 supplement 算不算，而是**正文到第 22 页才结束**。即使把第 23–30 页全部单独拆出去，主文仍然太长。真正要做的是把正文压到大约 10 页，再把 references 控制到 1.5–2 页左右。

依据如下：

1. **IEEE Author Center 明确允许 supplementary material 作为独立文件上传。**  
   IEEE 官方作者中心写的是：supplementary files 应标记为 supplementary，并在投稿时作为 separate files 上传；接受后，这些 supplemental files 会被压缩并随文章上传到 IEEE Xplore。citeturn277489view0  
   这说明 IEEE 期刊系统层面是支持独立 supplementary file 的。

2. **JBHI 旧规则/编辑部回复明确：放在 manuscript 末尾的 Supplement 算页数。**  
   一个公开问答引用了 JBHI 页面：regular paper 页数上限 12 页，且 “including supplementary material”；同一问答里作者转述编辑部回复：supplementary material 如果 added at the end of your manuscript，也会 included in the page limit。citeturn277489view1  
   这条虽然不是 JBHI 官网原文，但它很关键：**不能把 Supplement 塞在主 PDF 后面来规避页数。**

所以对你这篇的实际建议是：

**不要把 Supplement 放在 main.pdf 里。** 你现在第 23–30 页的 Appendix / Supplementary Material 应该拆成单独文件上传。你的主文 PDF 只保留正文、关键图表和 references。fileciteturn0file0

但我不建议你把希望完全寄托在 Supplement 不算页数上，因为你这篇**即使删掉第 23–30 页，正文+references 仍然到第 22 页**。JBHI regular paper 更现实的目标还是：

**main manuscript 控制到 12 页以内；Supplement 单独上传。**

你可以按这个边界处理：

| 内容 | 放哪里 |
|---|---|
| 核心方法、ASS 定义、tier rule | 主文 |
| Table X per-model audit summary | 主文 |
| 1AVB anchor、BBB positive、AFIB artifact、SBRAD heterogeneity | 主文 |
| Hyperparameters、multi-seed、完整 ablation、operator battery、SBRAD diagnostic | 独立 Supplement |
| Appendix 里的 reproducibility details | 独立 Supplement 或 GitHub/Zenodo |

一句话：**JBHI/IEEE 应该允许独立 supplementary file 上传；但你不能把它放在主稿末尾，并且主稿本身仍必须大幅压缩。**

依据分两层：

**1. IEEE 总规则：补充材料应作为 separate files 上传。**  
IEEE Author Center 明确说 supplementary files should be labeled as supplementary and uploaded as separate files during article submission，支持 PDF、DOC、TXT、图片、视频等格式。也就是说，从 IEEE 投稿机制上，**独立 supplementary file 是允许的**。citeturn829235search0

**2. 但 JBHI 自己的页数规则以前写得很严：regular paper 12 页上限 including supplementary material。**  
我没法直接打开 JBHI 官网页面，因为 embs.org/jbhi 被 robots.txt 阻止了；但公开引用的 JBHI 作者指南内容写的是：regular paper page limit is 12 pages，**including supplementary material**。同一页面还提到 regular paper 超过 8 页有 mandatory overlength page charges。citeturn112905search0

所以实际操作上，我建议你按这个策略：
